properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued October 12 at 7:08PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from Craig Key to Halfmoon Shoal
out 20 nm...
Gulf of America from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal
out to 5 fathoms...

At 707 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists detected a a
strong thunderstorm, capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots.
This thunderstorm was located near Big Pine Shoal, moving southwest
at 10 knots.

Locations that will be affected include...
Looe Key Light and Big Pine Shoal.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.
properties.area: Gulf of America from West End of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out to 5 Fathoms; Hawk Channel from Craig Key to west end of Seven Mile Bridge out to the reef; Hawk Channel from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out to the reef; Straits of Florida from Craig Key to west end of Seven Mile Bridge out 20 NM; Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of Halfmoon Shoal out 20 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 4:05PM PDT until October 12 at 7:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Clark County in southern Nevada, including
Valley of Fire State Park...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 405 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Overton and Valley Of Fire.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued October 12 at 6:27PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Mona Passage Southward to 17N...

* At 627 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and possible
waterspouts. This strong thunderstorm was located about 15 miles
northeast of Mona Island, moving west at 10 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Mona Passage Southward to 17N.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and possible waterspouts. Boaters should
seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 12 at 12:54PM EDT until October 12 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...Portions of Alexander, Catawba, and Iredell Counties, along
the shores of Lookout Shoals Lake.

* WHEN...Until 900 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas including
residential yards, docks, and boat-launch areas is ongoing along
the shores of Lookout Shoals Lake. Residents should take immediate
actions to protect property adjacent to the lake and monitor
messaging from county Emergency Management agencies.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1245 PM EDT, Levels of the lakes of the Catawba River remain
elevated as water continues to move downriver following the heavy
rain event over the weekend. While Lookout Shoals Lake has
receded since Sunday afternoon, it remains at Action stage and
some flooding of low-lying areas near the lake shore could
continue through at least this Monday evening.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. Please obey all barricades and heed any evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.area: Alexander, NC; Catawba, NC; Iredell, NC
